$comment: Rails for the pr-medic's ORCHESTRATOR session, added by `ralph.sh` with
`--settings` because `roles.ts` names this file as the role's
`claude-orchestrator-settings.json` — so it repeats every rule of that
file, and adds the medic's own.
The medic writes to the operator's branch, and the one way it may is
re-read of the pull request, the diff guard, the `Pr-Medic` trailer and a
lease pinned to the sha it read. A raw `git push` skips all four, so it is
denied here; `push.ts`'s own `git push` is a child of `bun`, which no Bash
Both spellings, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`, for the reason
`claude-executor-settings.json` gives. Like that file's path rules it is a
tripwire, not a boundary: `git -C . push` or `/usr/bin/git push` would go
round it. What it catches is the habit: a session that reaches for the
push every coder makes is refused and pointed back at the fence.
